items.title: Show HN: Eight: a symbolic, indentation-based programming language
items.contentSnippet:
Eight is a symbolic, indentation-based programming language that compiles to C11.
It reads UTF-32 source files (with BOM) and emits standard C code, which is then compiled with Clang, GCC, or TCC. The language has no keywords: instead, it uses a system of punctuation symbols that combine by meaning.
Here is the standard "Hello, World!" entry point in Eight:
$f "main" :
    !> "Hello, World!"
    !^ 0
!@f "main"
